title: Find the trend signal
brief:
Your antenatal clinic introduced a phone-reminder system to lift **ANC fourth-visit completion**. The chart shows the last 16 weeks (median = 51%).

Using Provost & Murray's **trend rule** — five or more consecutive points all going up (or all going down) signal a non-random change — click the points that make up the trend.

(Keyboard users: press Tab to enter the chart, Left/Right arrow to move between points, Enter to select.)

task.stem: Click each point that is part of the trend (the run of consecutive points all moving in the same direction). Submit when you have the full trend selected.

debrief.correct: Spotted. Weeks 7–12 rise every single week — 41 → 48 → 54 → 60 → 66 → 71 — that is **six** consecutive increasing points, which meets the trend rule (five or more). The run clearly *starts* at week 7 (week 6 → week 7 is a drop) and *ends* at week 12 (week 12 → week 13 falls back). Direction, not level, is the signal: it is the sustained climb that tells you the reminder system is changing the system, not any single week's value.
debrief.wrong: The trend rule: **five or more consecutive points all going up, or all going down.** Find where the line climbs without interruption — weeks 7 to 12 rise every week (41 → 48 → 54 → 60 → 66 → 71). The pre-run wobble (weeks 1–6) and the plateau after week 12 are not part of the trend. Count the *direction* of each step, not how high the points are.
debrief.rule_cited: Provost & Murray (2nd ed.) — Trend rule (≥ 5 consecutive points all increasing or all decreasing). Call it at the fifth point; do not wait for the slope to flatten.
